Theme

Travel & transport

shortcut noun

also short cut, take a shortcut, shorter way

classical

Cic. Off. 2.43: via ad glōriam proxima et quasi compendiāria (Lewis & Short)

via compendiāria

a short cut, a shorter way

In Cicero figurative; the feminine alone, compendiāria (via understood), is Varro’s, Petronius’ and Seneca’s.

Other words

  • compendiāria, compendiāriae f.

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Petr. 2.9; Sen. Ep. 119.1 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 378: compendāria

    Traupman prints compendāria; the word is compendiārius, from compendium.

Examples

  • compendiāriā īre

    to take a shortcutTraupman 378

SourcesLewis & Short: compendiarius

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 378.
